The article focused on former White House adviser Steve Bannon, who had been indicted on wire-fraud and money-laundering conspiracy charges related to the “We Build the Wall” fundraising campaign. Prosecutors alleged that the campaign diverted hundreds of thousands of dollars in donations for personal expenses. Bannon was awaiting trial when Trump pardoned him, so the allegations had not been resolved in a criminal trial. The pardon removed the possibility of federal prosecution for the covered conduct but did not establish whether the allegations were true. existing_copy_for_context_only.frozen_synopsis: Every time President Trump traveled to one of his private clubs or hotels, taxpayer money flowed into his personal businesses.
